newsitem.title: CHINA: New underground for China capital late, over cost.
newsitem.headline: New underground for China capital late, over cost.

text.p: The Chinese capital is trying to raise money to cover the cost of the expansion of its underground railway, already far over budget and long overdue, officials said on Thursday.

The project, due for completion at the end of 1997, was now not expected to be finished until late 1999 due to difficulties raising capital, an official with the Beijing Mass Transit Railway Corp said.

The Beijing municipal government was trying to find new channels to raise capital in addition to a $162 million Japanese government loan and a 2.0 billion yuan loan from the State Development Bank, he said.
He declined to give details of how the city would raise the funds, or to say whether it would issue debt.

The cost of the 12.7 km extension of China's two-line underground railway system had soared to 6.0 billion yuan by the end of 1996, up from an initial budget of 2.5 billion when construction began in 1990.
The city also hopes to add three more lines by 2010 to expand the length of the system by 62.8 km.
